answer: Agents submit a signed ciphertext (cipher) of a unique timber‑derived proof‑of‑work hash; the network timestamps it on a rolling tide ledger and then forces every new juror to issue a cross‑examination challenge that requires the prover to reveal a fresh nonce within one block. The prover must lock up a stake of 10 tokens per identity and wait the full tide interval (≈5 minutes) before the challenge expires, otherwise the stake is forfeited. An attacker therefore pays 10 tokens and a 5‑minute lock‑up for each fake identity, making mass Sybil creation prohibitively costly.
